title: Kernel finiteness from local generating epimorphisms
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and $U\subseteq X$ open. Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal H$ be a morphism of module sheaves on the open slice over $U$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $q$ be local generating data for $\mathcal F$: objects $V_i$ covering the terminal object of that slice and generating epimorphisms $p_i:\mathcal O_{V_i}^{\oplus I_i}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F|_{V_i}$, with no finiteness assumption on $I_i$. If $\ker(\varphi|_{V_i}\circ p_i)$ is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent] for every $i$ (composition in categorical order: first $p_i$, then $\varphi|_{V_i}$), then $\ker\varphi$ is of finite type on the slice over $U$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BY (lemma-coherent-abelian), proof of (2), second paragraph: kernel is the image of the composite from local free relations; Lemma 01B7 (lemma-extension-finite-type), part (1), and Definition 01B5 (definition-finite-type). Verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01BY.

proof.text: Work on the open slice over U. The private over_preserves_kernel helper proves that overFunctor preserves the kernel of phi: reflect the mapped kernel cone through SheafOfModules.forget and evaluate on each object of the slice; the resulting cone is the original kernel cone mapped by evaluation followed by restriction of scalars along the identity. Mathlib evaluation preserves finite limits. This identifies the restricted kernel with kernel(phi.over V).

For a commutative square p then f = g then j in any abelian category, with p epi and j mono, the private epi_kernel_of_epi helper proves kernel.map g f p j comm is epi. Refine a map into kernel f so that its composite with kernel.ι f lifts through p. Its lift a satisfies a then g then j = 0; cancel the mono j to show a then g = 0. Factor a through kernel g, and cancel kernel.ι f to check the lifting equation. Apply this general square lemma with g = p then f and j the identity. This directly supplies the local kernel quotient without importing the ringed-space section-lifting theorem.

The private finiteType_of_epi helper works for an arbitrary category site, with independent coefficient, object and morphism universes (not just a small site in the coefficient universe). It pushes local generating families through restrictions of an epimorphism using Mathlib GeneratingSections.ofEpi. The restriction functor is a left adjoint (overPushforwardOverAdj), hence preserves epimorphisms; the finite generating index sets are unchanged. Apply this to the preceding epi and to the inverse kernel restriction isomorphism. The hypothesis h supplies the finite type source on each member of the chosen cover.

The private finiteType_of_cover helper permits an arbitrary covering-index universe. Choose finite local generators on each member of the cover and index the flattened cover by the dependent sum of their index types. Mathlib CoversTop.over proves that it covers. pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence for Over.iteratedSliceEquiv transports the generators from the twice-restricted module; its counit identifies this with the once-restricted module. GeneratingSections.map and ofEpi preserve the finite index type. Shrink the resulting LocalGeneratorsData to the site universe using LocalGeneratorsData.shrink; each generating family is one of the original finite families. These data prove that kernel phi is finite type. Empty covers and empty generating families are included by these constructions. The public theorem specializes the generic private finiteType_kernel_of_local_generators helper, with explicit sheafification instances on the iterated slices.

theorem finiteType_kernel_local_generators (X : RingedSpace.{u})
    (U : Opens X) {F H : SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X).over U)}
    (φ : F ⟶ H) (q : SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData.{u, u, u, u} F)
